issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double (see UML lines), but the solution implementation declares and returns an int (public int getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor()). This return-type mismatch leads to inconsistent expectations: students guided by the problem/UML will implement a method returning double, while the reference solution returns int and performs integer division. This can cause confusion about the correct return type and produce incorrect results due to integer division.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution implementation match the UML: change the method signature to public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() and return a double value, e.g. return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors(); Alternatively, if an integer result was intended, update the UML and problem text to specify an int return type and clarify integer division semantics.
